hubs.name: hub_business_entity
hubs.description: Company-wide party register (customers, vendors, employees, persons). A person is a business entity with no separate identifier, so persons share this hub rather than getting a hub of their own. Email, phone and credential relations are also keyed by BusinessEntityID and feed this hub.

hubs.name: hub_address
hubs.description: Postal address, recorded once and shareable by many parties.

hubs.name: hub_address_type
hubs.description: Reference list of address types (Billing, Home, Shipping).

hubs.name: hub_contact_type
hubs.description: Reference list of contact roles a person plays for an organisation.

hubs.name: hub_phone_number_type
hubs.description: Reference list of phone number kinds (home, work, mobile).

hubs.name: hub_country_region
hubs.description: Country or region identified by ISO code.

hubs.name: hub_state_province
hubs.description: State or province identified by its own number.

hubs.name: hub_department
hubs.description: Register of departments, the organisational units where people work. Keyed on the stable DepartmentID because department names can change.

hubs.name: hub_shift
hubs.description: Register of eight-hour working shifts. Keyed on the stable ShiftID because shift names and times can be adjusted.

hubs.name: hub_job_candidate
hubs.description: Job candidates: people who applied for a position and whose application HR holds.

hubs.name: hub_product
hubs.description: Product (finished goods, components, sub-assemblies). Anchored on ProductID because every production relation (inventory, work orders, BOM, cost/price history, transactions, reviews) references products by ProductID; the day-to-day ProductNumber is carried in sat_product_details.

hubs.name: hub_product_category
hubs.description: Top level of the merchandising hierarchy; name held in satellite.

hubs.name: hub_product_subcategory
hubs.description: Second level of the product classification hierarchy.

hubs.name: hub_product_model
hubs.description: Product model at which design, catalogue content and manufacturing instructions are held.

hubs.name: hub_culture
hubs.description: Language/locale designation identified by a short culture code.

hubs.name: hub_unit_measure
hubs.description: Standard unit of measure used for size, weight and BOM quantities.

hubs.name: hub_product_description
hubs.description: Library entry of a free-text marketing description.

hubs.name: hub_product_photo
hubs.description: Library entry of a product photograph.

hubs.name: hub_illustration
hubs.description: Technical diagram used in manufacturing instructions.

hubs.name: hub_document
hubs.description: Entry (folder or document) in the controlled document library, identified by its hierarchy node.

hubs.name: hub_location
hubs.description: Manufacturing location / inventory holding location; referenced by LocationID in inventory and routing.

hubs.name: hub_work_order
hubs.description: Work order raised to manufacture a product.

hubs.name: hub_work_order_operation
hubs.description: Operation within a work order, identified by work order plus operation sequence.

hubs.name: hub_scrap_reason
hubs.description: Standard scrap reason.

hubs.name: hub_inventory_transaction
hubs.description: Inventory movement; live and archive stores feed the same hub so they form one continuous history.

hubs.name: hub_product_review
hubs.description: Customer-submitted product review.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order
hubs.description: Purchase order placed with a vendor, identified by its purchase order number.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order_detail
hubs.description: Purchase order line, identified by the purchase order plus its line number.

hubs.name: hub_ship_method
hubs.description: Shipping method for inbound purchases. Keyed on ShipMethodID, the identifier purchase orders reference (REQ-022-2), so orders can join to it. The shipping company name is kept in a satellite.

links.name: link_address_state_province
links.description: The state or province in which an address sits; country is derived via the state.

links.name: link_state_province_country_region
links.description: Each state or province belongs to exactly one country or region.

links.name: link_business_entity_address
links.description: Party-address relationship in a given capacity (address type); unique by party, address and type.

links.name: link_business_entity_contact
links.description: Organisational contact relationship: an organisation (BusinessEntityID), the person acting as its contact (PersonID) and the contact role; unique by all three.

links.name: link_business_entity_department_shift
links.description: Employee assignment to a department and shift over time, from EmployeeDepartmentHistory. The employee has one current assignment at a time, so the employee is the driving key.
links.unit_of_work: BusinessEntityID + DepartmentID + ShiftID: one assignment of an employee to a department and shift (start date tracked in the effectivity satellite)

links.name: link_job_candidate_business_entity
links.description: Links a job candidate record to the employee hired from it. If a link exists, the candidate was hired.
links.unit_of_work: JobCandidateID + BusinessEntityID: a candidate hired as an employee

links.name: link_product_subcategory
links.description: Product placed in (at most one) subcategory.

links.name: link_product_subcategory_category
links.description: Subcategory belongs to exactly one category.

links.name: link_product_model
links.description: Product belongs to at most one product model.

links.name: link_product_unit_measure
links.description: Units of measure in which a product's size and weight are expressed.

links.name: link_product_model_description_culture
links.description: Model described by a product description in a specific culture; the three-way combination is the business fact.

links.name: link_product_model_illustration
links.description: Illustrations supporting product models (many-to-many).

links.name: link_product_product_photo
links.description: Photographs used for products (many-to-many).

links.name: link_product_document
links.description: Documents applying to products (many-to-many).

links.name: link_document_business_entity
links.description: Document owner (employee, sourced from Document.Owner) joined to the existing HR business entity hub.

links.name: link_bill_of_materials
links.description: Component-in-assembly relationship between two products, with the unit of the component quantity.

links.name: link_product_location
links.description: Inventory holding of a product at a location.

links.name: link_work_order_product
links.description: Product being made by a work order.

links.name: link_work_order_scrap_reason
links.description: Scrap reason recorded on a work order (optional).

links.name: link_work_order_routing
links.description: Operation of a work order, the product manufactured and the location where it is performed.

links.name: link_inventory_transaction_product
links.description: Product involved in an inventory transaction.

links.name: link_product_review_product
links.description: Product a review relates to.

links.name: link_product_vendor
links.description: Vendor-product supply relationship: which vendor supplies which product, and the unit of measure it is bought in. Many-to-many.
links.unit_of_work: ProductID + vendor BusinessEntityID (with the UnitMeasureCode the product is bought in)

links.name: link_purchase_order
links.description: Purchase order header: the vendor the order is placed with, the employee who created it, and the shipping method it names.
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID with VendorID, EmployeeID and ShipMethodID from one order header

links.name: link_purchase_order_detail
links.description: Purchase order line: the order it belongs to and the product it refers to.
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID with the line's ProductID

links.name: link_purchase_order_detail_product
links.description: Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderDetail.ProductID references PRODUCTID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

links.name: link_purchase_order_business_entity
links.description: Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID references BUSINESSENTITYID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_details
satellites.description: Business entity register change timestamp; rowguid excluded as replication-only technical metadata.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_name
satellites.description: Person name details with full history.
satellites.split_rationale: Ordinary personal name data; carries the Person last-modified timestamp (held in this satellite only).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_type
satellites.description: Primary person type classification code.
satellites.split_rationale: Classification used for wide aggregated reporting; changes at a different rate from names.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_consent
satellites.description: Email promotion (marketing consent) preference with full history for compliance audit.
satellites.split_rationale: Compliance-sensitive consent tracked independently of name changes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_sensitive
satellites.description: Sensitive XML additional contact information and demographics, access-restricted.
satellites.split_rationale: Data classification: sensitive personal data restricted separately; XML data type.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_email
satellites.description: A person's email addresses, numbered within the person, with history.
satellites.split_rationale: Own source relation at finer grain (several per person).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_phone
satellites.description: A person's telephone numbers qualified by phone number type, with history.
satellites.split_rationale: Own source relation at finer grain (several per person).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_credential
satellites.description: Existence and last-change date of a sign-in credential only; hash and salt are never loaded.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source; credential values excluded for security.

satellites.name: sat_address_details
satellites.description: Street, city and postal details of an address with full history.

satellites.name: sat_address_location
satellites.description: Geographic coordinates of an address for mapping and territory analysis.
satellites.split_rationale: Spatial data type and personal-data classification differ from street details.

satellites.name: sat_address_type_details
satellites.description: Address type descriptive name.

satellites.name: sat_contact_type_details
satellites.description: Contact type descriptive name.

satellites.name: sat_phone_number_type_details
satellites.description: Phone number type name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_country_region_details
satellites.description: Country or region name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_details
satellites.description: State or province ISO code, no-genuine-code flag and name.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_territory
satellites.description: Sales territory assignment of a state or province, historised; territory descriptions come from the sales area.
satellites.split_rationale: Territory reassignment changes at a different rate and drives historical roll-ups.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_address_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of the party-address relationship.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_details
satellites.description: Employee attributes that can be widely reported: network login, job title, hire date, salaried/hourly flag, active flag and last-updated timestamp. History is kept because the source overwrites these values.
satellites.split_rationale: Non-sensitive employee classification attributes from Employee that change slowly; rowguid is excluded as a technical column

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_sensitive
satellites.description: Restricted personal employee data: national ID, date of birth, gender and marital status. Access is limited to authorised HR users.
satellites.split_rationale: Split out by data classification (PII) so access can be restricted

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_leave
satellites.description: Available vacation and sick-leave balances, kept as a series of point-in-time readings.
satellites.split_rationale: High rate of change compared with other employee attributes

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_hierarchy
satellites.description: The employee's position and level in the corporate hierarchy. Changes are captured because the source holds only the current position.
satellites.split_rationale: Hierarchy position changes independently of other attributes and supports reconstructing past structures

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_pay
satellites.description: Employee pay rate history: one row per effective rate-change date, with the hourly rate and pay frequency.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source relation at finer grain (one row per rate change), so modelled as multi-active; EmployeePayHistory is now declared as a feed of hub_business_entity

satellites.name: sat_department_details
satellites.description: Department name, group membership and last-changed date, with history kept for as-was reporting.

satellites.name: sat_shift_details
satellites.description: Shift definition (name, start and end time), with history kept so past shift hours stay understandable.

satellites.name: sat_job_candidate_resume
satellites.description: The candidate's résumé as a structured document, plus its last-updated timestamp.
satellites.split_rationale: Candidate personal data about non-employees, subject to its own retention rules

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of each department/shift assignment. An open end date marks the current assignment.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_details
satellites.description: Last-updated timestamp of each assignment record, one row per assignment start date, used to spot stale records.
satellites.split_rationale: The effectivity satellite carries only the start and end dates, so the audit timestamp sits in its own satellite. It is multi-active on StartDate because repeat assignments to the same department and shift are separate rows.

satellites.name: sat_product_details
satellites.description: Descriptive product attributes including the natural product number.
satellites.split_rationale: Slowly changing descriptive attributes.

satellites.name: sat_product_pricing
satellites.description: Current standard cost and list price on the product record.
satellites.split_rationale: Changes more frequently than descriptive attributes.

satellites.name: sat_product_inventory_policy
satellites.description: Inventory planning parameters.
satellites.split_rationale: Planning parameters change independently.

satellites.name: sat_product_lifecycle
satellites.description: Sale availability and discontinuation dates.
satellites.split_rationale: Lifecycle events change on their own cadence.

satellites.name: sat_product_cost_history
satellites.description: Standard cost periods per product.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source at finer grain (product + start date).

satellites.name: sat_product_list_price_history
satellites.description: List price periods per product.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source at finer grain (product + start date).

satellites.name: sat_product_category_details
satellites.description: Category name.

satellites.name: sat_product_subcategory_details
satellites.description: Subcategory name.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_details
satellites.description: Product model name.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_content
satellites.description: Structured catalogue description and manufacturing instructions.
satellites.split_rationale: Large structured-document data type, inclusion to be confirmed.

satellites.name: sat_culture_details
satellites.description: Culture name.

satellites.name: sat_unit_measure_details
satellites.description: Unit of measure name.

satellites.name: sat_product_description_details
satellites.description: Marketing description text.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_details
satellites.description: Photo file names.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_image
satellites.description: Binary photo images.
satellites.split_rationale: Binary data type, inclusion to be confirmed.

satellites.name: sat_illustration_details
satellites.description: Structured technical diagram.

satellites.name: sat_document_details
satellites.description: Document metadata: title, folder flag, hierarchy depth, file, revision, engineering change, status, summary.

satellites.name: sat_document_content
satellites.description: Full binary document content.
satellites.split_rationale: Binary data type, inclusion to be confirmed.

satellites.name: sat_location_details
satellites.description: Location name, hourly cost rate and capacity hours.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_details
satellites.description: Work order quantities and dates.

satellites.name: sat_scrap_reason_details
satellites.description: Scrap reason failure description.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_operation_details
satellites.description: Scheduled/actual dates, resource hours and costs of an operation.
satellites.split_rationale: WorkOrderRouting is unique on WorkOrderID + ProductID + OperationSequence; ProductID distinguishes concurrent rows per operation key.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_details
satellites.description: Live-store transaction details; order reference kept as identifiers read with transaction type until sales/purchasing areas exist.
satellites.split_rationale: Split by source system: live store.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_archive
satellites.description: Archived transaction details, same information as the live store.
satellites.split_rationale: Split by source system: archive store.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_details
satellites.description: Review date, rating and comments.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_reviewer_pii
satellites.description: Reviewer identity (personal data).
satellites.split_rationale: PII classification split.

satellites.name: sat_product_location_inventory
satellites.description: Quantity on hand per shelf and bin; history built by capture over time.

satellites.name: sat_bill_of_materials_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of a component in an assembly.

satellites.name: sat_bill_of_materials_details
satellites.description: Component quantity per assembly and BOM level.
satellites.split_rationale: BillOfMaterials is unique on ProductAssemblyID + ComponentID + StartDate; StartDate distinguishes concurrent rows per link key.

satellites.name: sat_product_product_photo_details
satellites.description: Principal-image flag for a product photograph.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_details
satellites.description: Vendor identifying and descriptive attributes: account number, company name and purchasing web service address (may be empty).
satellites.split_rationale: Slowly changing descriptive attributes, kept apart from the classification codes that change more often.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_status
satellites.description: Vendor credit rating, preferred status and active flag, with history so a vendor's state when an order was placed can be rebuilt.
satellites.split_rationale: Coded classification attributes whose history is explicitly required; they change at a different rate from the name and account details.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_terms
satellites.description: Agreed supply terms: average lead time, standard price, and minimum/maximum order quantities (the min/max meaning must be confirmed, REQ-022). History is kept for trend analysis.
satellites.split_rationale: Negotiated terms that change rarely, kept apart from the running receipt and on-order figures.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_receipt
satellites.description: Running operational figures: last receipt cost, last receipt date and quantity currently on order.
satellites.split_rationale: Fast-changing running values, separated from the agreed terms by rate of change.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_details
satellites.description: Order status, revision number, order date and estimated ship date, with history of status changes and revisions.
satellites.split_rationale: Lifecycle and status attributes, kept apart from the financial totals.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_totals
satellites.description: Order-level financial totals: subtotal, tax, freight and total due.
satellites.split_rationale: Monetary amounts, split from the status attributes by data type.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_detail_order
satellites.description: Ordered terms on each line: quantity ordered, unit price, line total and due date.
satellites.split_rationale: Values set when the order is placed, which rarely change afterwards.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_detail_receipt
satellites.description: Cumulative received, rejected and accepted quantities on each line. History shows how they progress, including partial deliveries.
satellites.split_rationale: Receipt and inspection progress changes over the life of the order, separately from the ordered terms.

satellites.name: sat_ship_method_details
satellites.description: Shipping company name (the business identifier). The rowguid replication column is left out because it has no business meaning.
satellites.split_rationale: Stable descriptive name, kept apart from the rates.

satellites.name: sat_ship_method_rates
satellites.description: Ship base (minimum charge) and ship rate (charge per pound), with history so historical freight can be checked against the rates in force at the time.
satellites.split_rationale: Commercial rates with required history, which change at a different rate from the name.

evidence: Customer.AccountNumber is 'number identifying the customer assigned by the accounting system', an alternate identifier of the customer concept.
No existing hub has a customer account number key. hub_business_entity is keyed by BusinessEntityID, which is a different identifier.
Customer.CustomerID is the primary key of its own table. No existing hub is keyed by CustomerID.
Customer.PersonID and Customer.StoreID reference BusinessEntityID. That makes customer a separate account concept pointing at a business entity, not the same key.
No mapping table says CustomerID equals BusinessEntityID.

Store.BusinessEntityID is a BusinessEntityID, the same identifier name and format as hub_business_entity's key. The hub is already fed by Person, Employee and Vendor from the shared BusinessEntityID space.
The column comment says 'Foreign key to Customer.BusinessEntityID', but Customer has no such column. The comment looks mistaken, which lowers confidence.
The merge rests on the key match only. A reviewer should confirm that Store keys come from the BusinessEntity population.
SalesOrderNumber is a computed unique identifier derived from SalesOrderID. It is an alternate key of the sales order concept.
The only existing order hub is hub_purchase_order, which is keyed by PurchaseOrderID. That is a procurement order, not a sales order.
SalesOrderHeader.SalesOrderID is the primary key of a sales order. The vault only has hub_purchase_order (PurchaseOrderID), a different business key and process (vendor purchasing).
No cross-reference links SalesOrderID to PurchaseOrderID.
SalesOrderDetail is keyed by SalesOrderID + SalesOrderDetailID. The existing hub_purchase_order_detail is keyed by purchase_order_line and belongs to purchase orders.
No cross-reference links the two.
SalesPerson.BusinessEntityID comment: 'Foreign key to Employee.BusinessEntityID'. This is an explicit cross-reference.
Employee already feeds hub_business_entity, which is keyed by BusinessEntityID.
SalesTerritory.TerritoryID is the primary key of a sales territory. No existing hub models territories.
hub_state_province and hub_country_region are different concepts. SalesTerritory only references CountryRegionCode as an FK.
SalesTerritory.Name is a descriptive name or alternate identifier of the new territory concept.
No existing hub models territories, and a shared 'Name' stem is not evidence of a match.
CreditCard.CreditCardID is the primary key of its own table. No existing hub is keyed by a credit card identifier.
PersonCreditCard only links it to BusinessEntityID.
CardNumber is an alternate identifier of the credit card concept. No existing hub holds it.
It is also sensitive data, so the human reviewer should decide whether it is used as a business key.
Currency.CurrencyCode is the ISO currency code and the primary key of Currency. No existing hub is keyed by a currency code.
hub_country_region (CountryRegionCode) and hub_unit_measure (UnitMeasureCode) are different code lists.
CurrencyRate.CurrencyRateID is the primary key of the exchange rate table. No existing construct models exchange rates.
This is the natural composite key of an exchange rate: date plus from and to currency. No existing construct models exchange rates.
It is an alternate key to CurrencyRateID for the same new concept.
SpecialOffer.SpecialOfferID is the primary key of a promotion or discount. No existing hub models promotions.
SalesReason.SalesReasonID is the primary key of a reason lookup for sales. The existing hub_scrap_reason is keyed by ScrapReasonID and is a different concept; a shared 'reason' stem is not evidence.
ShoppingCartItem is a new online-shopping concept, keyed by ShoppingCartID (nvarchar) and ShoppingCartItemID. No existing hub models carts.
SalesTaxRate.SalesTaxRateID is the primary key of tax rates. No existing hub models tax rates.
This composite is an alternate key of the tax rate concept. StateProvinceID is only a reference to hub_state_province.
The tax rate is not the state or province itself, so it is not a merge with hub_state_province.
CountryRegionCurrency.CountryRegionCode comment: 'Foreign key to CountryRegion.CountryRegionCode'. SalesTerritory.CountryRegionCode says the same.
It is the same ISO code and the same name as the business key of hub_country_region.

requirements.text: The business must have a consolidated, historical view of sales activity for reporting, performance management and planning.

References from sales data to products, people and business entities, employees, addresses, shipping methods, and countries/regions and states/provinces maintained in other domains must be preserved so sales information can later be joined to those areas.
The business must identify every customer by the customer account number assigned by the accounting system, which uniquely identifies the customer.
The business must distinguish an individual-person customer from a store customer.
For an individual customer, the business must retain the reference to the person who is the customer.
For a store customer, the business must retain the reference to the store.
The business must know the sales territory in which each customer is located.
The business must know when a customer's record was last changed in the operating system, so that reporting can be reconciled against the source.
The business must be able to report the customer base by territory.
The business must be able to report the customer base by customer kind (individual vs. store).
The business must identify each store by its business entity reference.
The business must record the store name of each store.
The business must know which sales representative is assigned to each store.
The business must retain the store demographics captured for each store, covering number of employees, annual sales and store type.
The business must be able to segment reseller performance by store demographic characteristics such as store size or store type.
The business must identify every sales order by its unique sales order number.
The business must know which customer placed each order.
The business must know whether an order was placed online by the customer or entered by a sales representative, as this distinguishes the two sales channels.
For orders not placed online, the business must know which sales representative created the order.

The business must know the territory in which each sale was made, recorded on the order itself, and reporting must be explicit about whether the order territory, the customer's territory or the representative's current territory is meant, since all three are held separately.
The business must track the date each order was created.
The business must track the date each order is due to the customer.
The business must track the date each order was shipped.
The business must track the current status of an order using the operational status values: in process, approved, backordered, rejected, shipped, cancelled.
The business must be able to measure order fulfilment performance, i.e. whether orders shipped on or before their due date.
The business must retain the customer's own purchase order number where the customer supplied one.
The business must retain the financial accounting number reference carried on the order, to allow reconciliation with finance.
The business must know the billing address used for each order.
The business must know the shipping address used for each order, as a piece of information separate from the billing address.
The business must know the shipping method chosen for each order.
The business must retain sales representative comments recorded against an order, as context for enquiries and disputes.
The business must be able to report order counts and values by channel, by territory, by representative, by customer and by period.
The business must track the revision number of an order, an incremental number tracking changes to the order over time, so it can tell that an order has been amended and how many times.
The business must record the order subtotal, described as the sum of the line totals for the order.
The business must record the tax amount charged on the order.
The business must record the freight (shipping cost) charged on the order.
The business must record the total due from the customer, described as subtotal plus tax plus freight.
The business must be able to analyse revenue with tax and freight separated from product revenue.
The business must know which credit card was used to pay for an order, where a card was used.
The business must retain the credit card approval code provided by the card company, for payment reconciliation and dispute handling.
The business must be able to report the share of orders paid by card versus those with no card recorded.
The business must know which currency exchange rate was applied to each order, where the order was not in the company's base currency.
The business must be able to report sales both in the transaction currency and converted to a reporting currency, using the rate that applied to the order.
requirements.obj: sales in transaction and reporting currency

requirements.text: The business must identify each order line within its order, using one incremental unique number per product sold.
The business must know which product was sold on each order line.
The business must know the quantity ordered per product on each order line.
The business must know the unit selling price of the product on each order line.
The business must know the discount amount applied to each order line.
The business must know the line total, described as unit price × (1 − discount) × quantity.
The business must know which special offer (promotional code) applied to each order line, so that promotional effectiveness can be measured.
The business must retain the shipment tracking number supplied by the shipper for each order line, because lines of one order may ship separately.
The business must be able to analyse sales by product, by quantity, by realised price and by discount level.
requirements.obj: sales by product, quantity, price and discount

requirements.text: The business must be able to distinguish list-price revenue from discount given away, at order line level.
The business must maintain the catalogue of sales reasons, each with a description.
Each sales reason must belong to a reason category.
The business must know which sales reasons were recorded against each order; an order may have several reasons and a reason may apply to many orders.
The business must be able to report order volume and value by sales reason and by reason category.
requirements.obj: orders by sales reason and category

requirements.text: The business must be able to report the proportion of orders for which no sales reason was recorded, as a data-quality measure.
The business must identify each sales representative by their business entity reference, which is also their employee reference.
The business must know the territory a sales representative is currently assigned to.
The business must know each representative's projected yearly sales quota.
The business must know the bonus due to a representative if the quota is met.
The business must know the commission percentage a representative receives per sale.
The business must know the representative's year-to-date sales total and previous-year sales total as maintained by the operational system.
The business must be able to compare a representative's actual sales against quota and identify who is on track to earn the bonus.
The business must be able to report sales by representative over time, independently of the running totals held in the operational system.
The business must maintain the catalogue of sales territories, each with a territory name.
The business must know the country or region each territory belongs to.
The business must know the geographic group a territory belongs to, so that results can be rolled up regionally.
The business must know each territory's year-to-date sales and previous-year sales.
The business must know each territory's year-to-date business costs and previous-year costs.
The business must be able to report territory contribution, i.e. sales against costs, for the current and previous year.
The business must be able to roll territory results up to geographic group and to country/region.
The business must maintain the register of credit cards used for payment, identified by the card record held in the operational system.
The business must know the card type (card name), the card number, and the expiry month and year of each credit card.
The business must be able to report sales by card type.
Access to credit card numbers and expiry data, which are sensitive personal and payment information, must be restricted.
The business must state whether the card number is needed at all in the warehouse or whether a masked or partial value is sufficient.
The business must know which credit cards belong to which person; a person may hold several cards and a card may be associated with more than one person.
The business must be able to identify cards used on orders that are not registered to the ordering customer, as an input to fraud and data-quality review.
requirements.obj: cards used on orders not registered to the ordering customer

requirements.text: The business must retain shopping cart items, each identified within its shopping cart.
The business must know the shopping cart identifier for each cart item.
requirements.obj: shopping cart identifier of cart item

requirements.text: The business must know the product for each cart item.
The business must know the quantity ordered for each cart item.
The business must know the date and time each cart item was created.
requirements.obj: creation date and time of cart item

requirements.text: The business must be able to report which products are added to carts and in what quantities.
requirements.obj: products added to carts and quantities

requirements.text: The business must be able to measure cart activity over time, using the creation date of cart items.
The business must maintain the catalogue of special offers, each with a discount description.
The business must know each special offer's discount percentage.
The business must know each special offer's discount type category.
requirements.obj: discount type category of special offer

requirements.text: The business must know the group the discount applies to, such as Reseller or Customer, so that promotions can be reported per channel.
The business must know each special offer's minimum quantity threshold.
The business must know each special offer's maximum quantity threshold.
The business must know each special offer's start date.
The business must know each special offer's end date, i.e. the end of the period during which it is valid.
The business must be able to determine which special offers were valid at any given date, including offers that have since expired, so that historical orders can be explained.
requirements.obj: special offers valid at a given date

requirements.text: The business must be able to report revenue and discount attributable to each special offer, and to each offer type and category.
requirements.obj: revenue and discount per special offer, offer type and category

requirements.text: The business must know which products each special offer applies to.
A special offer may cover many products, and a product may be covered by several special offers.
The business must be able to check that the offer recorded on an order line was applicable to the product on that line, as a data-quality and pricing-governance control.
requirements.obj: applicability of order line offer to product

requirements.text: The business must maintain the list of currencies, identified by their ISO currency code, with the currency name.
The business must be able to present currency names in reporting rather than raw codes.
The business must retain exchange rates as a time series, recording for each rate the date and time the rate was obtained, the currency converted from, and the currency converted to.
The business must retain the average exchange rate for the day.
requirements.obj: average exchange rate for the day

requirements.text: The business must retain the final (end-of-day) exchange rate, as average and end-of-day rates serve different reporting purposes.

The business must be able to reproduce the exchange rate that was actually applied to a given order, not merely today's rate, so that historical reporting is stable and does not change when rates move.
The business must be able to report the same sales figures in more than one currency.
The business must state which of the two rates (average or end-of-day) is used for each report.
requirements.obj: exchange rate type used per report

requirements.text: The business must be able to identify orders where no exchange rate was recorded and understand how those are to be treated (presumed base currency).
The business must know which currencies are used in which countries/regions.
A country/region may be associated with more than one currency, and a currency with more than one country/region.
The business must be able to check that sales in a given country/region were transacted in a currency valid for that country/region.
requirements.obj: validity of sales currency for country/region

requirements.text: The business must maintain the register of sales tax rates, each with a tax rate description.
The business must know the state, province or country/region each tax rate applies to.
The business must know the tax type for each rate, using the operational meanings: applied to retail transactions, applied to wholesale transactions, or applied to all sales.
The business must know the tax rate amount.
The business must be able to report tax collected by jurisdiction and by tax type.
requirements.obj: tax collected by jurisdiction and tax type

requirements.text: The business must be able to compare the tax amount charged on an order with the tax rates applicable to the relevant jurisdiction, as a compliance check.
requirements.obj: order tax amount with applicable tax rates

requirements.text: A sales order is placed by exactly one customer, and a customer may place many orders over time.
A sales order is handled by at most one sales representative, orders placed online by the customer have no representative, and a representative handles many orders.
A sales order is made in one sales territory, and a territory carries many orders.
A sales order consists of one or more order lines, and each order line belongs to exactly one order.
An order line sells one product, and a product is sold on many order lines.
An order line may be sold under one special offer, and an offer is used on many order lines.
A sales order may cite several sales reasons, and a sales reason may be cited on many orders.
A sales order may be paid with one credit card, and a card may be used on many orders.
A credit card may be registered to one or more people, and a person may hold several cards.
A sales order may use one currency exchange rate, and a rate may apply to many orders.
requirements.obj: sales order and currency exchange rate

requirements.text: A customer is located in one sales territory, and a territory contains many customers.
A customer is either a person or a store.
A reseller store is served by one sales representative, and a representative serves many stores.
A sales representative is currently assigned to at most one territory.
A sales representative has worked a series of territories over time.
A sales territory belongs to one country/region and to one geographic group.
A special offer applies to one or more products, and a product may be covered by several offers.
A country/region may trade in several currencies, and a currency may be used in several countries/regions.
An exchange rate converts from one currency to another on a given day.
A sales tax rate applies to one state/province or country/region for a given tax type.
A shopping cart contains one or more cart items, each for one product.
There is no recorded link from a shopping cart to a customer or to an order.
A sales order carries a billing address and a shipping address, which may differ.
A sales order is shipped using one shipping method.
The business must retain the full history of sales quotas per sales representative, including the quota date and the quota amount in force from that date.
The business must be able to determine the quota that applied to a sales representative at any point in the past.
requirements.obj: historical sales quota of a representative

requirements.text: The business must be able to compare the quota that applied to a representative in a past period with the sales actually achieved in that period.
The business must be able to report how a representative's quota has moved over time.
requirements.obj: quota movement over time per representative

requirements.text: The business must be able to report how often a representative's quota was revised.
The representative record carries a single current quota figure alongside the dated quota history, and the business must be aware of this duality.
Reporting must state whether it uses the current quota figure or the dated quota history.
The current quota figure and the dated quota history must be reconcilable with each other.
The business must retain the history of which representative worked which territory, including the date the representative started work in the territory and the date they left.
A representative's territory assignment is open-ended while they are still working the territory, with no end date recorded.
The business must be able to identify the currently active territory assignment for each representative.
The business must be able to determine who was responsible for a territory on any given date.
requirements.obj: representative responsible for a territory on a date

requirements.text: Historical sales must be credited to the representative who actually held the territory at the time of the sale.
requirements.obj: historical sales to territory holder at the time

requirements.text: The business must be able to see the sequence of representatives who have held a territory.
The business must be able to see how long each representative held a territory.
The representative record carries the currently assigned territory alongside the dated assignment history, and the business must be aware of this current-versus-historical duality.
Where an order's territory differs from the representative's territory at the time of the order, the business must be able to see that difference.
requirements.obj: difference between order territory and representative territory

requirements.text: Where an order's territory differs from the representative's territory at the time of the order, the business must be able to explain that difference.
requirements.obj: difference between order territory and representative territory

requirements.text: Exchange rates are a daily time series, and the business needs the rate as at the relevant date.
requirements.obj: exchange rate as at relevant date

requirements.text: Exchange rates must never be retrospectively overwritten in reporting.
Special offers have explicit start and end dates.
The business must be able to determine the special offers that were live at any date, including expired ones.
requirements.obj: special offers live at a given date

requirements.text: The business must be able to see how descriptive information changes over time where it matters commercially, in particular a customer's territory, a store's assigned representative, a store's demographics, a special offer's discount percentage, and a territory's group.
requirements.obj: changes in descriptive information over time

requirements.text: Every record in this area carries a last-modified date and time.
The business needs the last-modified date and time as the primary signal that something has changed.
requirements.obj: last modified date as change signal

requirements.text: The business needs the last-modified date and time as the basis for reconciling warehouse content with the operational system.

For all other entities in this area, the operational system holds only the current state, so history for those entities can only be built from the point the warehouse starts capturing it, and the business must accept this.
requirements.obj: history of entities holding only current state

requirements.text: The business must decide for which entities holding only current state it is worth building history.
requirements.obj: entities for which history is built

requirements.text: The business must be able to report sales value and volume by period, territory, geographic group, country/region, representative, customer, customer kind, product, channel, currency, special offer and sales reason.
The business must be able to compare actual sales against quota per representative and per period, including the bonus and commission implications.
The business must be able to report territory profitability using sales and cost figures at territory level.
The business must be able to measure discounting: total discount given, by offer, by product, by channel and by customer kind.
The business must be able to measure fulfilment: order-to-ship elapsed time, on-time-against-due-date performance, and the distribution of order statuses.
The business must be able to measure channel mix: online orders versus representative-entered orders, in volume and value.
The business must be able to report tax and freight separately from product revenue.
The business must be able to report sales in a single reporting currency across all territories, using the rate that applied to each order.
requirements.obj: sales in a single reporting currency

requirements.text: The business must be able to analyse the reseller base by store demographics and by assigned representative.
The business must be able to analyse online cart activity by product and period, within the limits of the missing link from shopping cart to customer or order.

The business must be able to see, for each order, whether the key commercial attributes are present: customer, territory, representative (where not online), currency rate (where non-base currency), and payment reference.
requirements.obj: presence of key commercial attributes on orders

requirements.text: The business must be able to check that the order total agrees with the sum of its lines plus tax and freight, and to report where it does not.
requirements.obj: order total against lines plus tax and freight

requirements.text: The business must be able to check that line totals agree with quantity, unit price and discount as described by the source.
requirements.obj: line totals against quantity, unit price and discount

requirements.text: The business must be able to report orders referencing a special offer that is outside its validity period at the order date.
requirements.obj: orders with special offer outside validity period

requirements.text: Once the open question on customer type is resolved, the business must be able to report customers that are neither a person nor a store, or that are both.
requirements.obj: customers that are neither or both person and store

requirements.text: The business must be able to report representatives with no territory on any given date.
The business must be able to report territories with no representative on any given date.

The business must be able to reconcile operationally maintained running totals (representative and territory year-to-date and last-year figures) against totals recalculated from orders, and to report material differences.
requirements.obj: operational running totals against recalculated order totals

requirements.text: Each entity in this area must have a named business owner who is accountable for its definitions and for resolving the clarifications in the document.
Business owners must be assigned before the warehouse is built; they have not yet been assigned.
Credit card data (card number, expiry, card type, holder association) is payment-sensitive, and its handling, retention and access rules must be defined before it is loaded.
requirements.obj: credit card data handling, retention and access rules

requirements.text: Individual customers are natural persons, and personal-data handling rules, including retention limits and the treatment of deletion requests, must be defined for the customer information in this area.
requirements.obj: personal-data handling rules for customer information

requirements.text: Sales representative quota, bonus, commission and achievement figures are remuneration data about identifiable individuals and must be access-restricted to those with a legitimate need.
Store demographics are commercially sensitive information about reseller partners and must be treated as confidential.
The replication identifier carried by several records has no business meaning and is not required by the business, but may be retained as a technical trace of the source record.
Values computed by the operational system (order number, customer account number, line total, order subtotal and total due) must be taken as given from the source rather than recalculated.
Values computed by the operational system must be checkable by the business.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-003 states the business identifies every customer by the account number assigned by the accounting system, which uniquely identifies the customer. It is business-recognised and unique; REQ-054-3 says it is computed by the source and taken as given.
CustomerID is a system-generated surrogate that the requirements do not call an identifier. REQ-003 prefers the account number, so this is a weak key kept only as a technical fallback.
REQ-011 states the business identifies each store by its business entity reference. It is stable, unique and recognised across domains (REQ-002).
REQ-016 states every sales order is identified by its unique sales order number, a business-facing value that REQ-054-3 says is taken as given from the source.
SalesOrderID is the system-generated order identifier and a weak surrogate-style key. REQ-016 prefers SalesOrderNumber, but SalesOrderID is the order's parent reference on lines and reason links.

REQ-044 identifies an order line within its order using one incremental unique number per product sold. It is only unique together with the parent order (REQ-042-2), so it forms a composite key with the sales order number.
REQ-059 states each sales representative is identified by their business entity reference, which is also their employee reference. It is stable, unique and not nullable.

REQ-067 and REQ-060 require a territory catalogue, and orders, customers and representatives reference territories by this identifier. The requirements name no explicit business identifier, so TerritoryID is the available key. Name (REQ-067) is an alternative.
REQ-067 says each territory has a territory name. The requirements do not call it unique or stable, so it is a weaker alternative.

REQ-074 states the card register is identified by the card record held in the operational system. The card number (REQ-075) is sensitive (REQ-077, REQ-049-3), so the record identifier is preferred even though it is system-assigned.
REQ-075 lists the card number as an attribute. It is business-recognised, but REQ-077 and REQ-078 restrict access and question whether it is needed at all, so it is a poor hub key.
REQ-021-2 states currencies are identified by their ISO currency code. The code is stable, unique, standard and not nullable.

REQ-048-2 says orders reference a rate and REQ-023-2 treats rates as a time series. CurrencyRateID is a system-assigned identifier. A composite of rate date, from currency and to currency (REQ-023-2, REQ-057-2) is the natural alternative.
REQ-023-2 and REQ-057-2 describe a rate by the date it was obtained, the currency converted from and the currency converted to. Together these identify one rate in the daily series (REQ-019-3).

REQ-008-2 requires a catalogue of special offers, and order lines reference the offer (REQ-050). SpecialOfferID is the only identifier among the known columns. REQ-050 calls it a promotional code, but no unique business code is stated.
REQ-054 requires a catalogue of sales reasons, and orders cite them (REQ-056). No business code is named, so the identifier is the available key. Name is an alternative.

REQ-001-2 and REQ-002-2 say each cart item is identified within its shopping cart, with the cart identifier known for each item. This suggests a composite key. The ID is system-generated, hence the moderate score.

REQ-033-2 requires a tax rate register, and REQ-058-2 says a rate applies to one state/province or country/region for a given tax type. SalesTaxRateID is a system-generated identifier. A composite of StateProvinceID and TaxType is the natural alternative.

REQ-058-2 says a tax rate applies to one state/province or country/region for a given tax type, and REQ-034-2 and REQ-035-2 support this. The requirements do not state that this combination is unique.

REQ-002, REQ-068 and REQ-030-2 refer to countries/regions, linked to territories and currencies. CountryRegionCode is the known source column. The entity is maintained in another domain, but the code is stable and widely recognised.

hubs.name: hub_business_entity
hubs.description: Company-wide party register (customers, vendors, employees, persons). A person is a business entity with no separate identifier, so persons share this hub rather than getting a hub of their own. Email, phone and credential relations are also keyed by BusinessEntityID and feed this hub.

hubs.name: hub_address
hubs.description: Postal address, recorded once and shareable by many parties.

hubs.name: hub_address_type
hubs.description: Reference list of address types (Billing, Home, Shipping).

hubs.name: hub_contact_type
hubs.description: Reference list of contact roles a person plays for an organisation.

hubs.name: hub_phone_number_type
hubs.description: Reference list of phone number kinds (home, work, mobile).

hubs.name: hub_country_region
hubs.description: Country or region identified by ISO code.

hubs.name: hub_state_province
hubs.description: State or province identified by its own number.

hubs.name: hub_department
hubs.description: Register of departments, the organisational units where people work. Keyed on the stable DepartmentID because department names can change.

hubs.name: hub_shift
hubs.description: Register of eight-hour working shifts. Keyed on the stable ShiftID because shift names and times can be adjusted.

hubs.name: hub_job_candidate
hubs.description: Job candidates: people who applied for a position and whose application HR holds.

hubs.name: hub_product
hubs.description: Product (finished goods, components, sub-assemblies). Anchored on ProductID because every production relation (inventory, work orders, BOM, cost/price history, transactions, reviews) references products by ProductID; the day-to-day ProductNumber is carried in sat_product_details.

hubs.name: hub_product_category
hubs.description: Top level of the merchandising hierarchy; name held in satellite.

hubs.name: hub_product_subcategory
hubs.description: Second level of the product classification hierarchy.

hubs.name: hub_product_model
hubs.description: Product model at which design, catalogue content and manufacturing instructions are held.

hubs.name: hub_culture
hubs.description: Language/locale designation identified by a short culture code.

hubs.name: hub_unit_measure
hubs.description: Standard unit of measure used for size, weight and BOM quantities.

hubs.name: hub_product_description
hubs.description: Library entry of a free-text marketing description.

hubs.name: hub_product_photo
hubs.description: Library entry of a product photograph.

hubs.name: hub_illustration
hubs.description: Technical diagram used in manufacturing instructions.

hubs.name: hub_document
hubs.description: Entry (folder or document) in the controlled document library, identified by its hierarchy node.

hubs.name: hub_location
hubs.description: Manufacturing location / inventory holding location; referenced by LocationID in inventory and routing.

hubs.name: hub_work_order
hubs.description: Work order raised to manufacture a product.

hubs.name: hub_work_order_operation
hubs.description: Operation within a work order, identified by work order plus operation sequence.

hubs.name: hub_scrap_reason
hubs.description: Standard scrap reason.

hubs.name: hub_inventory_transaction
hubs.description: Inventory movement; live and archive stores feed the same hub so they form one continuous history.

hubs.name: hub_product_review
hubs.description: Customer-submitted product review.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order
hubs.description: Purchase order placed with a vendor, identified by its purchase order number.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order_detail
hubs.description: Purchase order line, identified by the purchase order plus its line number.

hubs.name: hub_ship_method
hubs.description: Shipping method for inbound purchases. Keyed on ShipMethodID, the identifier purchase orders reference (REQ-022-2), so orders can join to it. The shipping company name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_customer
hubs.description: A customer (individual person or store), identified by the customer account number assigned by the accounting system.

hubs.name: hub_sales_order
hubs.description: A sales order, identified by its unique sales order number.

hubs.name: hub_sales_order_line
hubs.description: A sales order line, identified within its order by an incremental line number.

hubs.name: hub_sales_territory
hubs.description: A sales territory in the territory catalogue.

hubs.name: hub_credit_card
hubs.description: A credit card in the payment card register, identified by its operational card record.

hubs.name: hub_currency
hubs.description: A currency identified by its ISO currency code.

hubs.name: hub_currency_rate
hubs.description: A daily currency exchange rate, identified by rate date, from-currency and to-currency.

hubs.name: hub_special_offer
hubs.description: A special offer (promotion) in the offer catalogue.

hubs.name: hub_sales_reason
hubs.description: A sales reason in the sales reason catalogue.

hubs.name: hub_shopping_cart_item
hubs.description: A shopping cart item, identified within its shopping cart.

hubs.name: hub_sales_tax_rate
hubs.description: A sales tax rate for a jurisdiction and tax type.

links.name: link_address_state_province
links.description: The state or province in which an address sits; country is derived via the state.

links.name: link_state_province_country_region
links.description: Each state or province belongs to exactly one country or region.

links.name: link_business_entity_address
links.description: Party-address relationship in a given capacity (address type); unique by party, address and type.

links.name: link_business_entity_contact
links.description: Organisational contact relationship: an organisation (BusinessEntityID), the person acting as its contact (PersonID) and the contact role; unique by all three.

links.name: link_business_entity_department_shift
links.description: Employee assignment to a department and shift over time, from EmployeeDepartmentHistory. The employee has one current assignment at a time, so the employee is the driving key.
links.unit_of_work: BusinessEntityID + DepartmentID + ShiftID: one assignment of an employee to a department and shift (start date tracked in the effectivity satellite)

links.name: link_job_candidate_business_entity
links.description: Links a job candidate record to the employee hired from it. If a link exists, the candidate was hired.
links.unit_of_work: JobCandidateID + BusinessEntityID: a candidate hired as an employee

links.name: link_product_subcategory
links.description: Product placed in (at most one) subcategory.

links.name: link_product_subcategory_category
links.description: Subcategory belongs to exactly one category.

links.name: link_product_model
links.description: Product belongs to at most one product model.

links.name: link_product_unit_measure
links.description: Units of measure in which a product's size and weight are expressed.

links.name: link_product_model_description_culture
links.description: Model described by a product description in a specific culture; the three-way combination is the business fact.

links.name: link_product_model_illustration
links.description: Illustrations supporting product models (many-to-many).

links.name: link_product_product_photo
links.description: Photographs used for products (many-to-many).

links.name: link_product_document
links.description: Documents applying to products (many-to-many).

links.name: link_document_business_entity
links.description: Document owner (employee, sourced from Document.Owner) joined to the existing HR business entity hub.

links.name: link_bill_of_materials
links.description: Component-in-assembly relationship between two products, with the unit of the component quantity.

links.name: link_product_location
links.description: Inventory holding of a product at a location.

links.name: link_work_order_product
links.description: Product being made by a work order.

links.name: link_work_order_scrap_reason
links.description: Scrap reason recorded on a work order (optional).

links.name: link_work_order_routing
links.description: Operation of a work order, the product manufactured and the location where it is performed.

links.name: link_inventory_transaction_product
links.description: Product involved in an inventory transaction.

links.name: link_product_review_product
links.description: Product a review relates to.

links.name: link_product_vendor
links.description: Vendor-product supply relationship: which vendor supplies which product, and the unit of measure it is bought in. Many-to-many.
links.unit_of_work: ProductID + vendor BusinessEntityID (with the UnitMeasureCode the product is bought in)

links.name: link_purchase_order
links.description: Purchase order header: the vendor the order is placed with, the employee who created it, and the shipping method it names.
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID with VendorID, EmployeeID and ShipMethodID from one order header

links.name: link_purchase_order_detail
links.description: Purchase order line: the order it belongs to and the product it refers to.
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID with the line's ProductID

links.name: link_purchase_order_detail_product
links.description: Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderDetail.ProductID references PRODUCTID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

links.name: link_purchase_order_business_entity
links.description: Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID references BUSINESSENTITYID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

links.name: link_customer_person
links.description: An individual customer and the person who is the customer.

links.name: link_customer_store
links.description: A store customer and the store it represents.

links.name: link_customer_sales_territory
links.description: The sales territory in which a customer is located.

links.name: link_store_sales_person
links.description: The sales representative assigned to a reseller store.

links.name: link_sales_person_sales_territory
links.description: The territory a sales representative is currently assigned to (from the representative record).

links.name: link_sales_person_territory_history
links.description: Dated history of territory assignments per sales representative.

links.name: link_sales_territory_country_region
links.description: The country/region a sales territory belongs to.

links.name: link_sales_order
links.description: The sales order header event: the order with its customer, representative, territory, billing and shipping addresses, ship method, credit card and currency rate.
links.unit_of_work: SalesOrderNumber with CustomerID, SalesPersonID, TerritoryID, BillToAddressID, ShipToAddressID, ShipMethodID, CreditCardID, CurrencyRateID

links.name: link_sales_order_line
links.description: An order line within its order, selling one product under a special offer.

links.name: link_sales_order_sales_reason
links.description: Sales reasons cited on an order (many-to-many).

links.name: link_business_entity_credit_card
links.description: Credit cards registered to persons (many-to-many).

links.name: link_currency_rate_currency
links.description: The from- and to-currency of an exchange rate.

links.name: link_country_region_currency
links.description: Currencies used in countries/regions (many-to-many).

links.name: link_sales_tax_rate_state_province
links.description: The state/province jurisdiction a tax rate applies to.

links.name: link_special_offer_product
links.description: Products covered by a special offer (many-to-many).

links.name: link_shopping_cart_item_product
links.description: The product in a shopping cart item.

links.name: link_sales_order_line_product
links.description: Declared foreign key SalesOrderDetail.ProductID references PRODUCTID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

links.name: link_sales_order_address
links.description: Declared foreign key SalesOrderHeader.BillToAddressID references ADDRESSID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

links.name: link_sales_order_business_entity
links.description: Declared foreign key SalesOrderHeader.SalesPersonID references BUSINESSENTITYID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

links.name: link_sales_order_ship_method
links.description: Declared foreign key SalesOrderHeader.ShipMethodID references SHIPMETHODID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_details
satellites.description: Business entity register change timestamp; rowguid excluded as replication-only technical metadata.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_name
satellites.description: Person name details with full history.
satellites.split_rationale: Ordinary personal name data; carries the Person last-modified timestamp (held in this satellite only).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_type
satellites.description: Primary person type classification code.
satellites.split_rationale: Classification used for wide aggregated reporting; changes at a different rate from names.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_consent
satellites.description: Email promotion (marketing consent) preference with full history for compliance audit.
satellites.split_rationale: Compliance-sensitive consent tracked independently of name changes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_sensitive
satellites.description: Sensitive XML additional contact information and demographics, access-restricted.
satellites.split_rationale: Data classification: sensitive personal data restricted separately; XML data type.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_email
satellites.description: A person's email addresses, numbered within the person, with history.
satellites.split_rationale: Own source relation at finer grain (several per person).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_phone
satellites.description: A person's telephone numbers qualified by phone number type, with history.
satellites.split_rationale: Own source relation at finer grain (several per person).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_credential
satellites.description: Existence and last-change date of a sign-in credential only; hash and salt are never loaded.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source; credential values excluded for security.

satellites.name: sat_address_details
satellites.description: Street, city and postal details of an address with full history.

satellites.name: sat_address_location
satellites.description: Geographic coordinates of an address for mapping and territory analysis.
satellites.split_rationale: Spatial data type and personal-data classification differ from street details.

satellites.name: sat_address_type_details
satellites.description: Address type descriptive name.

satellites.name: sat_contact_type_details
satellites.description: Contact type descriptive name.

satellites.name: sat_phone_number_type_details
satellites.description: Phone number type name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_country_region_details
satellites.description: Country or region name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_details
satellites.description: State or province ISO code, no-genuine-code flag and name.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_territory
satellites.description: Sales territory assignment of a state or province, historised; territory descriptions come from the sales area.
satellites.split_rationale: Territory reassignment changes at a different rate and drives historical roll-ups.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_address_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of the party-address relationship.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_details
satellites.description: Employee attributes that can be widely reported: network login, job title, hire date, salaried/hourly flag, active flag and last-updated timestamp. History is kept because the source overwrites these values.
satellites.split_rationale: Non-sensitive employee classification attributes from Employee that change slowly; rowguid is excluded as a technical column

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_sensitive
satellites.description: Restricted personal employee data: national ID, date of birth, gender and marital status. Access is limited to authorised HR users.
satellites.split_rationale: Split out by data classification (PII) so access can be restricted

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_leave
satellites.description: Available vacation and sick-leave balances, kept as a series of point-in-time readings.
satellites.split_rationale: High rate of change compared with other employee attributes

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_hierarchy
satellites.description: The employee's position and level in the corporate hierarchy. Changes are captured because the source holds only the current position.
satellites.split_rationale: Hierarchy position changes independently of other attributes and supports reconstructing past structures

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_pay
satellites.description: Employee pay rate history: one row per effective rate-change date, with the hourly rate and pay frequency.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source relation at finer grain (one row per rate change), so modelled as multi-active; EmployeePayHistory is now declared as a feed of hub_business_entity

satellites.name: sat_department_details
satellites.description: Department name, group membership and last-changed date, with history kept for as-was reporting.

satellites.name: sat_shift_details
satellites.description: Shift definition (name, start and end time), with history kept so past shift hours stay understandable.

satellites.name: sat_job_candidate_resume
satellites.description: The candidate's résumé as a structured document, plus its last-updated timestamp.
satellites.split_rationale: Candidate personal data about non-employees, subject to its own retention rules

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of each department/shift assignment. An open end date marks the current assignment.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_details
satellites.description: Last-updated timestamp of each assignment record, one row per assignment start date, used to spot stale records.
satellites.split_rationale: The effectivity satellite carries only the start and end dates, so the audit timestamp sits in its own satellite. It is multi-active on StartDate because repeat assignments to the same department and shift are separate rows.

satellites.name: sat_product_details
satellites.description: Descriptive product attributes including the natural product number.
satellites.split_rationale: Slowly changing descriptive attributes.

satellites.name: sat_product_pricing
satellites.description: Current standard cost and list price on the product record.
satellites.split_rationale: Changes more frequently than descriptive attributes.

satellites.name: sat_product_inventory_policy
satellites.description: Inventory planning parameters.
satellites.split_rationale: Planning parameters change independently.

satellites.name: sat_product_lifecycle
satellites.description: Sale availability and discontinuation dates.
satellites.split_rationale: Lifecycle events change on their own cadence.

satellites.name: sat_product_cost_history
satellites.description: Standard cost periods per product.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source at finer grain (product + start date).

satellites.name: sat_product_list_price_history
satellites.description: List price periods per product.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source at finer grain (product + start date).

satellites.name: sat_product_category_details
satellites.description: Category name.

satellites.name: sat_product_subcategory_details
satellites.description: Subcategory name.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_details
satellites.description: Product model name.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_content
satellites.description: Structured catalogue description and manufacturing instructions.
satellites.split_rationale: Large structured-document data type, inclusion to be confirmed.

satellites.name: sat_culture_details
satellites.description: Culture name.

satellites.name: sat_unit_measure_details
satellites.description: Unit of measure name.

satellites.name: sat_product_description_details
satellites.description: Marketing description text.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_details
satellites.description: Photo file names.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_image
satellites.description: Binary photo images.
satellites.split_rationale: Binary data type, inclusion to be confirmed.

satellites.name: sat_illustration_details
satellites.description: Structured technical diagram.

satellites.name: sat_document_details
satellites.description: Document metadata: title, folder flag, hierarchy depth, file, revision, engineering change, status, summary.

satellites.name: sat_document_content
satellites.description: Full binary document content.
satellites.split_rationale: Binary data type, inclusion to be confirmed.

satellites.name: sat_location_details
satellites.description: Location name, hourly cost rate and capacity hours.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_details
satellites.description: Work order quantities and dates.

satellites.name: sat_scrap_reason_details
satellites.description: Scrap reason failure description.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_operation_details
satellites.description: Scheduled/actual dates, resource hours and costs of an operation.
satellites.split_rationale: WorkOrderRouting is unique on WorkOrderID + ProductID + OperationSequence; ProductID distinguishes concurrent rows per operation key.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_details
satellites.description: Live-store transaction details; order reference kept as identifiers read with transaction type until sales/purchasing areas exist.
satellites.split_rationale: Split by source system: live store.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_archive
satellites.description: Archived transaction details, same information as the live store.
satellites.split_rationale: Split by source system: archive store.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_details
satellites.description: Review date, rating and comments.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_reviewer_pii
satellites.description: Reviewer identity (personal data).
satellites.split_rationale: PII classification split.

satellites.name: sat_product_location_inventory
satellites.description: Quantity on hand per shelf and bin; history built by capture over time.

satellites.name: sat_bill_of_materials_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of a component in an assembly.

satellites.name: sat_bill_of_materials_details
satellites.description: Component quantity per assembly and BOM level.
satellites.split_rationale: BillOfMaterials is unique on ProductAssemblyID + ComponentID + StartDate; StartDate distinguishes concurrent rows per link key.

satellites.name: sat_product_product_photo_details
satellites.description: Principal-image flag for a product photograph.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_details
satellites.description: Vendor identifying and descriptive attributes: account number, company name and purchasing web service address (may be empty).
satellites.split_rationale: Slowly changing descriptive attributes, kept apart from the classification codes that change more often.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_status
satellites.description: Vendor credit rating, preferred status and active flag, with history so a vendor's state when an order was placed can be rebuilt.
satellites.split_rationale: Coded classification attributes whose history is explicitly required; they change at a different rate from the name and account details.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_terms
satellites.description: Agreed supply terms: average lead time, standard price, and minimum/maximum order quantities (the min/max meaning must be confirmed, REQ-022). History is kept for trend analysis.
